name: Epistemic Foundations
crownClaim: Human knowledge acquisition through logic, perception, and induction is reliable enough to produce justified true beliefs about an external reality
instructions: Research each claim below. These are philosophical foundations -- some are axioms that cannot be empirically verified but are pragmatically indispensable. Score correspondence honestly (low for axioms). Focus evidence on SEP articles, key philosophical works, and psychophysics research where applicable.

claims.claim: An external reality exists independent of any observer's mind
A proposition and its negation cannot both be true simultaneously in the same respect
Human sensory perception, while fallible, systematically tracks features of external reality
Observed regularities in nature can be extrapolated to unobserved cases with justified (though defeasible) confidence
Valid deductive arguments preserve truth from premises to conclusions
Knowledge can be characterized as justified, true belief, subject to Gettier-type refinements
Human knowledge acquisition through logic, perception, and induction is reliable enough to produce justified true beliefs about an external reality

alternatives.claim: Only one's own mind can be known to exist; the external world may be an illusion
Systematic deception (evil demon, simulation) makes all sensory evidence unreliable
No amount of past observation can logically justify predictions about unobserved cases (Hume's problem remains unsolved)
